sections.preamble: You answer questions about a single medical image. Follow the answer format requested in the user message exactly.

content.text:
This is one axial slice of a T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI (radiological convention: patient right on image left, anterior at top). It contains a soft-tissue mass.

The left panel is the clean image; the right panel shows numbered marks. Choose the ONE mark that lies inside the tumor, as close to its centre as possible. End your reply with a final line exactly: ANSWER: <mark number>

The tumor is the bright, heterogeneous hyperintense mass on the image left, roughly spanning x 215-330 and y 320-430 in the left panel. In the right panel that corresponds to x ≈ 1000-1115.

Mark 450 sits at (1023, 387), which is inside the mass but near its lateral edge. Mark 473 sits at (1085, 341), at the upper margin of the mass. The mass center is around x ≈ 1055-1060, y ≈ 380, and no mark sits exactly there. Of the candidates, 450 is clearly within the bright tissue, while 473 may lie at the edge or in the bright rim.

In the left panel the bright region spans x ≈ 218-330 and y ≈ 325-430. Mark 473 maps to left-panel x ≈ 301, y ≈ 341, which is inside the bright region near its upper right. Mark 450 maps to x ≈ 239, y ≈ 387, which is also inside the bright region. The center is about (270, 378). The distance from 450 is about 31 px, and from 473 about 31-45 px (dx 31, dy 37, so about 48). That makes 450 closer.

ANSWER: 450
